title: Runtime release numbering and supported-lane policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a clear, operational semantic versioning and supported-release-lane policy for the serving runtime that minimizes surprise breaking changes, gives customers predictable upgrade windows, and ties rollout gating to telemetry signals and tooling. Scope: numbering scheme, classification of change types, supported lanes (long-term supported and current lanes), deprecation window durations, client compatibility headers, gating criteria for staged rollouts, automated migration tooling requirements, and rollback signal definitions. Out-of-scope: application-level SDK behavior (handled by SDK teams) except where headers or adapters are required for compatibility detection.
background: We have seen multiple customer upgrade disruptions from runtime changes that were nominally nonbreaking but had performance or behavioral regressions for certain workloads (KV cache semantics, adjusted kernel selection heuristics, and a recent tokenizer normalization change). Historically many runtime changes were communicated only via release notes; customers requested machine-readable signals, fixed deprecation windows, and an automated opt-in migration path. This policy aims to provide deterministic expectations for product, support, and customers so Dedicated/Private users can plan upgrades without unexpected service impact.
goals: Establish a release-numbering scheme that maps to compatibility expectations (major.minor.patch).
Define two supported lanes: Current (fast-evolving) and Supported (12-month maintenance lane) with clear promotion rules.
Classify change types with concrete examples and required mitigation steps.
Mandate rollout gates tied to telemetry thresholds and automated abort criteria.
Deliver a migration-helper CLI and an API header that allows client adapters to opt into 'compat mode' for transitional windows.
Specify deprecation windows and documentation/announcement requirements for each change class.
policy_summary: Versioning: Use semantic numbers where Major increments allow breaking changes and require migration support; Minor increments may include nonbreaking feature additions and opt-in behavioral changes; Patch is bugfix-only. Supported lanes: 'current' (latest minors, short runway) and 'supported' (selected minors from the last 12 months with security/critical fixes only). Deprecations: all deprecations must have a minimum 90-day announcement and a 180-day removal runway for noncritical changes in the current lane; supported lane deprecations require 270-day notice. Rollout gates: every change must define an automatic roll-out policy with preflight checks, staged traffic percentages, and telemetry thresholds (error rate, latency P95, model-output-regression metrics). Upgrade tooling: runtime must ship a migration-helper CLI (runtime-migrate) that can simulate binary-level behavior changes against a snapshot workload and produce a compatibility report. Compatibility headers: add X-Runtime-Compatible and X-Runtime-Depr to responses to help proxies and adaptors detect compatibility mode. Emergency rollback: an automated abort must trigger if aggregated error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase or latency P95 regresses > 25% in canary within 30 minutes.
change_classification: Breaking: any API signature, protocol, or binary ABI change that requires client code changes (examples: RPC contract change in control plane, removal of previously supported request fields). Requires major bump and migration plan.

Behavioral nonbreaking: semantics change that preserves contract but changes responses or timing (example: default batching policy changed). Requires minor bump, opt-in flag for one minor cycle, migration tests, and announcement.
Internal performance/implementation: kernel selection, optimizations that don't alter outputs. Patch allowed if covered by regression tests; must include performance telemetry during rollout.
Deprecation: explicit marker for fields/options slated for removal. Follow deprecation windows above and provide adapter shims where feasible.
rollout_gates: Canary: 0.5% traffic for 1 hour with tight telemetry collection.
Staged ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% over configurable windows, each stage requiring health checks to pass.
Auto-abort: defined thresholds on error-rate, latency P95, and output-regression metrics (model divergence).
Manual hold: product or security can place a hold; hold requires a runbook to resume.
telemetry_requirements: Preflight: must collect synthetic workload run and baseline metrics for latency, throughput, and representative output quality metrics.
Canary collection: require per-route P95 latency, error counts, throughput, and model-output divergence scores (where applicable).
Post-rollback analysis: collection of stack traces, request samples, and KV-cache hit/miss rates for 72 hours.
upgrade_tooling_requirements: runtime-migrate CLI that produces a deterministic compatibility report given a workload snapshot.
Adapter shim generator for common client languages to enable 'compat mode' toggles.
CI gates: every PR that changes runtime surface must include nightly migration checks against two representative workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc reviewed and approved by Eng Release Leads, Product, and Legal (security signoff recorded).
runtime CI adds migration check harness and a failing test where a breaking change occurs without a migration plan.
runtime-migrate prototype committed to tools repo and run against last two minors with generated reports.
Telemetry collection and auto-abort rules implemented in rollout service with configurable thresholds.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Adding more process may slow urgent bugfixes. Mitigation: allow emergency patches under a defined fast-path that still records a post-hoc migration summary. Risk: Customers on pinned private deployments may not accept automated headers. Mitigation: headers are opt-out via configuration in private deployments, but must be enabled for hosted and Dedicated by default.
